lines.note: Hikimiru is inspecting or testing a person. Initial F is damaged but fits both the alphabetic sequence and the following example.
Hito no kokoro o hiki miru is testing someone's heart or intentions. Idem indicates the same meaning as the preceding gloss.
Hikimogu is tearing off by force. The faint past ending oida is supported by the remaining type and the parallel NINJAL headword, not an invented separate o da.
Yubi o hikimogu gives fingers as the object of tearing off. The Portuguese arrancar continues at the row break.
Os dedos completes the finger example; this is a physical continuation of arrancar.
Hikimono is a musical instrument, qualified by Improp. The explanatory qualification limits the use rather than naming another instrument.
A second hikimono denotes a house's beams. Traves is a building term, unrelated to the music sense above.

runs.text: Couſa de comer que ſe reparte por

lines.note: The food sense of hikimono refers to something distributed among diners. The timing follows in the continuation.

runs.text: todos depois de estarem à meſa.

lines.note: Everyone is already at table before this food is distributed, completing the preceding definition.
The fourth hikimono is lathe-turned work, linking it to hiku's turning sense.
Hikimoyoosu is persuading or stirring others to action. Ex begins excitar, not executar, in the next row.

runs.text: citar a outros como pera ir ao campo, &c.

lines.note: Going out to the field is an example of the action encouraged. Citar completes excitar and resolves the OCR cutar.
Hikimukaeru means pulling or turning something to face another object. The following citation illustrates carts.

runs.text: couſa direita, ou de fronte doutra. Vt,

lines.note: The object is placed directly facing another; Ya- begins yagate in the cited Japanese sentence.

runs.text: gate Ioſephno von curumauo Iacobno võ

lines.note: Yagate Joseph no on kuruma o Jacob no on... describes Joseph's carriage relative to Jacob's. Biblical names are embedded in Japanese syntax and retain their printed Latin spellings.
Kuruma no mae e hikimukae tamaitsutsu brings the carriage before the other. The final tsutsu is split across physical rows.
The citation is to part 2 of Goſag. Logo begins the Portuguese rendering of the carriage movement.

runs.text: dear o carro de Ioſeph pera diante do carro de

lines.note: Joseph's carriage is turned in front of another carriage; the owner's name finishes on the next row.
Jacob completes the counterpart to Joseph. The middle c was an OCR d, not another proper name.
Hikimukeru means turning a thing by pulling it. Couſa is divided at the line end.
Virala completes the turning action with its attached feminine object pronoun.
Hikimusubu is tying one thing to another. A long-s type, not l, gives the intelligible musubu compound.
Yuori o hikimusubu is glossed as making a hut. The spelling Yuori is retained rather than silently changed to the expected iori.
Choupana, a hut, completes the example of constructing a shelter by binding material together.
Hikin is paraphrased as tobu tori, a flying bird. This is a separate Sino-Japanese noun amid hiki- compounds.
Hikinabikeru is bending or inclining, extended to inclining someone's heart in the next example.
Kokoro o hikinabikuru describes moving or winning over a heart. The old -kuru ending is preserved.
Mover o coração completes the figurative persuasion explanation.
Hikinarasu is making musical instruments sound. The repaired initial F avoids the nonsensical eikin arasu kana sequence.
Biwa no katachi o tsukuri describes making the shape of a biwa, followed by how it is strung.

runs.text: vmano vouo caqe fiqi naraxi, &c. Fox

lines.note: Uma no o o kake hiki narashi uses horse-tail hair as strings, then sounds the instrument. Fox. is a source label, not part of the sentence.

runs.text: ib. 4. Fazendo hũa forma de viola, &

lines.note: Book 4 is visibly cited, not a paragraph mark. The Portuguese begins making a viola-like form.

runs.text: pondo lhe ſedas de caualo por cordas a fez

lines.note: Horse hairs are put on it as strings. Sedas de cavalo describes that material, not silk cloth in this context.
Soar completes making the reconstructed instrument sound, corresponding to hiki narashi.
Hikinaosu is straightening something by pulling. The inflectional u has no secure accent to preserve from the OCR grave.

runs.text: xando, ou mudala a outro lugar.

lines.note: Moving the thing to another place is an alternative application of the same verb.
Hikinoberu is stretching by pulling. Its example comes from a Christian narrative rather than everyday clothing.

Iennhoninno xusocuuo fiqinobete xitani means stretching out the pious woman’s hands and feet, with xitani introducing what is placed beneath. Enlargement resolves the damaged second n in Iennhonin; NINJAL independently lists Iennhonin (zennyonin). The Portuguese Sancta supports that identification.
Hi o takase describes having a fire kindled. Part 1 of Goſag. is cited; the omitted i in fiuo was a meaningful OCR loss.

runs.text: tendendo os pes, & mãos da Sancta, & pon

lines.note: The Portuguese describes stretching the saint's feet and hands, confirming the Japanese limb pair.
Fire is placed below her. This finishes the narrative illustration of stretching, not a new entry.
Hikinoboseru is causing something to rise by pulling. Nobose is causative/transitive in this compound.
Hikinokoru is what remains in accounts. De begins depois in the following line.

runs.text: pois de deſcontar, ou deitar em deſpeſa, &c.

lines.note: The remainder follows deductions or expenditure. Deſcontar is visible and restores the accounting infinitive obscured by OCR.
Hikinokeru is setting aside or moving away, transitive in contrast with the next entry.
Hikinoku is moving oneself away. Its reflexive Portuguese equivalents differentiate it from hikinokeru.
Starſe completes afastar-se, the second reflexive equivalent. The line is a body continuation despite its short length.
Hikinoseru is pulling someone up onto a conveyance or seat. Embarkation begins the following gloss.
Putting someone aboard, on horseback, or higher up illustrates the causative sense of noseru.
Hikinuku is pulling out, as with trees. The damaged F was read as B by OCR.

runs.text: &c. ¶ Item, Arrancar, ou leuar do mõ-

lines.note: An additional application is drawing a weapon. Mõ- begins montante across the row boundary.
Montante and Catana identify weapons that can be drawn. Catana is embedded Japanese in Portuguese and remains available for typeface correction.
Hikyo is unreasonable conduct, paraphrased dori nai koto. Preserve the unmarked short vowel in this headword rather than borrowing the next entry's length mark.
Sem justiça completes the second equivalent, without justice, for the preceding unreasonable action.
Hikyō directs the reader to Fiqeô. Vide is italic editorial wording, not Japanese for kana conversion.

runs.text: Paßos de garganta, ou quebros da

lines.note: Hikyoku describes musical ornaments or fine turns of the voice. The Portuguese throat metaphor should not be read literally as steps.

runs.text: voz particulares, ou certas delicadezas como

lines.note: Particular vocal turns and refinements continue the musical explanation; delicadezas is a single word.
Fantesias in instrumental playing is the comparison. Hikyoku o tsukusu begins an example of musical mastery.

runs.text: Eſmerarſe na arte de cantar, ou tanger

lines.note: Tsukusu completes exhausting or perfecting one's art. Esmerar-se covers excellence in singing or instrumental performance.
Instrumento musico completes the object of playing and closes the musical entry.
Hikikiru is cutting or sawing by pulling. Qiri, not quri, supplies the cutting element and is visible in the scan.
Hikisagaru is falling behind while other people advance. The relative movement follows in the next row.
Outros diante finishes 'others ahead', explaining the backward position of the subject.
Hikisakeru here is tearing apart in an intransitive sense. The long-s type supplies saqe, not laqe.
Despedaçar-se completes the reflexive tearing explanation. The damaged vowel is read a in the verb, with uncertainty from the weak impression.
Hikisaku is the transitive counterpart, tearing something apart. Multiple damaged initial types caused the OCR raqa sequence.
Hikisarasu is dragging something out for public exposure. The following corpse example confirms sarasu rather than tarasu.
Kabane o hiki... introduces a corpse as the object of exposure; arrastando completes the Portuguese dragging action.
Sarasare continues the Japanese example. The Portuguese explicitly describes drawing out the dead body.

runs.text: deixalo no campo ſem ſer enterrado.

lines.note: The body is left in the open unburied, explaining the exposure sense without adding content to the diplomatic text.
Hikisobameru is drawing something toward one's side or moving it aside. Afastar is the Portuguese infinitive, not afaftar.

runs.text: pera algũa parte como quem foſſe pera tomar

lines.note: The illustrative scenario begins with someone going to take an object; the next line introduces the competing action.

runs.text: algũa couſa, & eu a tomaſſe primeiro, & afas-

lines.note: The speaker takes it first and moves it away. The subordinate tomaſſe prepares the parallel afastaſſe.
Moving it toward one's own side completes the scenario. Taſſe, not toſſe, completes the preceding verb.
Hikisobiku is dragging along, with hikojiru recommended as the better expression. The latter is printed in the italic gloss despite being Japanese.
Levar a rasto completes dragging; X labels regional usage in Ximo.
Hikisokonau is making a mistake while playing an instrument. The open-o inflectional marks are visible, and inſ- begins instrumento.

runs.text: trumento muſico. Item, per met. Encami-

lines.note: After the musical error sense, per met. introduces a figurative meaning of misleading someone.

runs.text: nhar mal, ou peruerter a alguem.

lines.note: Directing someone wrongly or corrupting them completes the figurative counterpart to faulty playing.
Hikisuguru is choosing or selecting, for example good people. The tall medial letter is long s, not i.
Other things can likewise be selected, completing the preceding entry's scope.
Hikisuteru is pulling out and discarding. The tçuru ending is part of the historical inflectional information.
Fora completes throwing something away or out, rather than a separate adverbial entry.
Hikisueru is pulling someone into position or seating them. The example below is coercive rather than ordinary hospitality.

runs.text: tar a alguem como preſo, ou malfeitor em algũ

lines.note: A prisoner or wrongdoer is placed at a particular location. The description qualifies whom the verb acts upon.
The location is for killing the prisoner, completing this historical usage example.

runs.text: Por ſe em feição de ſe aco

lines.note: Hikitatsu describes a group getting ready to withdraw or flee. Its full F initial is present despite the OCR omission.

runs.text: lher, ou fugir muita gente como do arrayal,

lines.note: Many people may flee from camp; the comma continues into the cited example rather than ending the entry.

Vǒjeino fiqitachitaru cuxe introduces the habitual retreat of a large body of people. Cuxe is くせ (癖), habit/custom: xe is the regular Jesuit spelling for セ, historically pronounced roughly シェ. This is not an anomalous x or an error for s/ſ. Likewise je regularly represents ゼ, historically roughly ジェ. The modern kana reading must not be used to modernize the printed consonant.
Nareba connects the cause; hitokaeshi mo kaesazu describes not turning them back even once. The divided Tai- begins the citation label.
Taifeiq., book 7, is the visibly printed citation form. The Portuguese begins explaining the tendency of a large group.

runs.text: gente que eſtã posta em fugida, não ouue faze-

lines.note: The people are already in flight, and could not be made to return. The construction continues into faze-los below.

runs.text: los tornar a tras, nem hũa ſò vez.

lines.note: Not even once could they be turned back. Só is a Portuguese limiting word, not fô, and the scan supports a long-s initial.
Hikitakuru is winding in a line by pulling it. The gloss continues at f195; the intervening de peſ- below is its repeated catchword, not an extra body continuation.
Catchword de peſ. anticipates de peſcar at the opening of f195. It is separated from body text without changing its stable ID.
